newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won closes down, Kia bail-out news hits.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won closes down, Kia bail-out news hits.

text.p: The won ended lower against the U.S. dollar on Tuesday as worries over the impact from financial troubles at the Kia Group sparked dollar buying, dealers said.
The won closed at 891.90, against the previous close on Monday of 891.40.

Without the Kia Group trouble, the won would have remained stronger on dollar supply from the $300 million global depositary receipt issue by Housing and Commercial Bank and on fears about the central bank's dollar sales, dealers said.
The Korea First Bank, the main creditor to Kia, said 18 of the group's 38 affiliates would be bailed out.
Fears about the fallout from the recent plunges of the Thai and Philippine currencies vis-a-vis the U.S. unit emerged again as the Kia Group news hit the market, dealers said.
"Now the sentiment toward the dollar is so strong that only the central bank's heavy dollar sales will be able to check the unit's strength," said a domestic bank dealer.
Dealers foresaw the won's base mid-rate would be pegged at 890.80 on Wednesday, against Tuesday's 891.40.
